source.title: Bootstrapping Parallel Anchors for Relative Representations
source.authors: Irene Cannistraci; Luca Moschella; Valentino Maiorca; Marco Fumero; Antonio Norelli; E. Rodolà

record.tranche_reason: The study extends relative-representation alignment to anchor discovery and evaluates it in word embeddings, vision encoders, and cross-lingual zero-shot stitching. It does not test convergence as model scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The study measures cross-model retrieval and stitching using relative representations and reports outcomes for ground-truth anchors (GT), seed anchors, and Anchor Optimization (AO). Rows below record the cross-model results; same-model diagonal entries are excluded because they do not measure alignment between independent models. Related-work claims are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study measures how well relative representations align independent models. It uses FastText vs Word2Vec, ViT-base vs ViT-small, and English vs Spanish RoBERTa for zero-shot stitching. Alignment is shown by retrieval and stitching scores with 300 ground-truth parallel anchors, 15 seed anchors, and AO-discovered anchors. These numbers bear on V4 (interchangeable representations via relative representations with little paired data). It is a methods paper, but its GT and seed comparators are direct alignment measurements, not only the method's own performance. No scale, seed, cross-modal or feature analyses.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say AO expands a small seed of parallel anchors and beats seed-only anchors. They report results comparable or superior to the full GT anchor set, with one order of magnitude fewer anchors. They also say it enables cross-lingual zero-shot stitching, and that removing the need for an initial seed is future work.
record.recipe_differences: Builds on relative representations and cosine-similarity anchors, but adds an optimization procedure that bootstraps additional parallel anchors from a small seed. This is not a direct reproduction of either original source's convergence experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported performance differs across word-embedding optimization direction, vision retrieval, and cross-lingual task/direction; retrieval outcomes are reported separately for Jaccard, MRR, and cosine. The study does not conduct a controlled sweep of similarity measures.
record.problems: The study covers limited model pairs and datasets and does not test scale or capability. It uses one stated similarity choice (cosine) rather than varying the similarity measure. Reported uncertainty is across five random seeds, while several results are averages over datasets; no broader uncertainty analysis is stated.
record.rows_left_out: Kept 58 of 78 cross-model method-by-metric results. Omitted the 12 ViT Seed and GT comparator results from Appendix A.3, Table 7, and the 8 cross-lingual GT results from Appendix A.2, Table 6, to stay within the 60-row limit. These comparator values are noted where relevant in the retained AO rows. Same-model diagonal entries were excluded because they do not measure cross-model alignment.

untested.parts: Linear or trained stitching maps; alignment with no paired data at all (AO still needs 15 parallel seed anchors); other similarity functions than cosine.
No systematic variation of similarity measure, K or input distribution.
No test of plateau or causes of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: Table 7 parsing: the Relative blocks appear in order AO, Seed, GT, each with Absolute diagonal blocks between them. The record took 1.00 diagonal values as GT; cross-model GT is Jaccard 0.10, MRR 0.23/0.28, cosine 0.97, so AO roughly matches GT in vision. Table 6 rows are decoder en {en, es} and decoder es {en, es}. The record shifted labels, putting same-model entries (en/en, es/es) into cross-lingual rows. The declared omissions (vision Seed/GT, cross-lingual GT) are the very comparators needed to judge V4 and should be restored as rows. Cosine between relative vectors stays high (0.85-0.97) even when retrieval fails, so it is not informative about alignment. Tiny paper; a single model pair per domain.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size, capability, or scale sweep; no test of whether alignment rises as models get larger or more capable.
No paired image-caption vision-language alignment experiment.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different initializations.

Tests relative representations with discovered parallel anchors for retrieval and zero-shot stitching; does not test linear maps, stitching layers generally, relative representations without paired anchors, or alignment without paired data.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Uses cosine similarity and reports Jaccard, MRR, cosine, F-score, and MAE outcomes, but does not vary the representation-similarity measure or systematically test sensitivity to its settings or input distribution.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data or objectives explain it.

relationships.condition: FastText vs Word2Vec relative representations with 300 GT or AO anchors, retrieval
relationships.reason: Cross-model MRR is 0.94-0.99, so words are almost always retrieved as their counterpart (R3, R4, R15, R16, R21, R22, R33, R34).
relationships.display_finding: Cross-model word retrieval achieved MRR 0.94–0.99 using 300 ground-truth or AO anchors.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: FastText vs Word2Vec relative representations with 300 GT or AO anchors, retrieval
source_check.reason: Tables 4–5 report cross-model MRR 0.94–0.99 with GT or AO, supporting near-complete counterpart retrieval in this condition.

relationships.condition: Word embeddings: neighbourhood structure, and only 15 parallel anchors
relationships.reason: Top-10 neighbourhood Jaccard is only 0.34-0.52 even with GT/AO (R1, R2, R13, R14, R31, R32). With 15 seed anchors alone, retrieval collapses (Jaccard 0.06, MRR 0.11-0.15; R7-R10, R25-R28).
relationships.display_finding: Top-10 neighborhood Jaccard reached only 0.34–0.52 even with GT/AO, while using 15 seed anchors alone reduced Jaccard to 0.06 and MRR to 0.11–0.15.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Word embeddings: neighbourhood structure, and only 15 parallel anchors
source_check.reason: Tables 4–5 report GT/AO Jaccard 0.34–0.52; Seed-only Jaccard is 0.06 and MRR 0.11–0.15. Interchangeability depends on the measure and anchor provision.

relationships.condition: ViT-base vs ViT-small on CIFAR-10 retrieval
relationships.reason: Even with all 300 GT anchors, cross-model Jaccard is about 0.10 and MRR 0.23-0.28 (Table 7). AO reaches only 0.11 and 0.27-0.28 (V1-V4), so the mapping is far from lossless.
relationships.display_finding: With all 300 GT anchors, cross-model Jaccard was approximately 0.10 and MRR 0.23–0.28, while AO reached only 0.11 and 0.27–0.28 respectively.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: FastText vs Word2Vec relative representations with 300 GT or AO anchors, retrieval
labels.reason: Tables 4–5 report cross-model MRR 0.94–0.99 with GT or AO, supporting near-complete counterpart retrieval in this condition.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Word embeddings: neighbourhood structure, and only 15 parallel anchors
labels.reason: Tables 4–5 report GT/AO Jaccard 0.34–0.52; Seed-only Jaccard is 0.06 and MRR 0.11–0.15. Interchangeability depends on the measure and anchor provision.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: ViT-base vs ViT-small on CIFAR-10 retrieval
labels.reason: Table 7 reports cross-model GT Jaccard 0.10 and MRR 0.23–0.28; AO Jaccard is 0.10–0.11 and MRR 0.27–0.28. Retrieval alignment remains incomplete.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Cross-lingual RoBERTa zero-shot stitching on Amazon Reviews
labels.reason: Table 6 reports cross-lingual weighted F1 0.46–0.48 with AO, 0.50–0.51 with GT and 0.41–0.44 with Seed; GT within-language F1 is 0.60–0.64. Stitching incurs substantial performance loss.

relation.reason: Cross-model retrieval and stitched downstream performance directly measure whether representations are interchangeable under V4.

tranche.reason: Tests relative-representation alignment in a limited-seed setting using anchor optimization, with retrieval and cross-lingual stitching results.

source_check.notes: The authors' conclusion paraphrase matches the text. R13's verdict-fix explanation misinterprets Jaccard: 0.52 is intersection over union, not the fraction of top-10 neighbours shared.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: FastText and Word2Vec retrieval with AO-discovered anchors
reader_labels.reason: AO improves on seed-only retrieval and reaches or exceeds the GT comparator on reported cross-model retrieval metrics (R13-R18, R31-R36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Vision retrieval and cross-lingual zero-shot stitching with AO
reader_labels.reason: Vision retrieval remains well below GT on Jaccard and MRR, and cross-lingual scores are generally below GT; vision cosine is unchanged from seed-only anchors (C1-C8, V1-V6).
